hints: Look at each statement as a separate mini test of acid-base chemistry, electron counting, shape, and complex formation.
Count the total electrons in $\text{NH}_4^+$ and in $\text{CH}_4$ carefully, remembering to subtract one electron for the 1+ charge.
Check the shape of $\text{NH}_4^+$ from its four bonding pairs, and recall which silver halides actually dissolve in ammonia to spot the only fully correct claim.
walkthrough:
**Test A: Ammonium ion plus acid or base?**

Ammonia is a base, so its conjugate acid $\text{NH}_4^+$ needs a base to remove $\text{H}^+$. Acid would just keep it as $\text{NH}_4^+$.

Chemical rule:
$$\text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Test B: Which silver halides dissolve in ammonia?**

Ammonia forms the complex $[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+$. Only $\text{AgCl}$ dissolves in dilute ammonia and $\text{AgBr}$ in concentrated ammonia.

Recall:
$$\text{AgI} \text{ is insoluble even in concentrated } \text{NH}_3$$

**Test C: Count electrons in ammonium and methane**

This is the key check. Count atomic electrons then adjust for charge.

Calculation:
$$\text{NH}_4^+: 7 (\text{N}) + 4 \times 1 (\text{H}) - 1 (\text{for + charge}) = 10$$
$$\text{CH}_4: 6 (\text{C}) + 4 \times 1 (\text{H}) = 10$$

**Test D: What is the shape of ammonium?**

$\text{NH}_4^+$ has 4 bonding pairs and no lone pairs on N, so it is tetrahedral, just like $\text{CH}_4$. It does contain a dative bond from $\text{NH}_3$ to $\text{H}^+$, but it is definitely not square planar.

Conclusion: Only the electron-count statement is fully correct.

options.A: False. Ammonia gas is released by warming an ammonium salt with a strong base (alkali), not an acid. Acid protonates any $\text{NH}_3$ to keep it as $\text{NH}_4^+$.
options.B: False. $\text{AgCl}$ is soluble in dilute $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{AgBr}$ only in concentrated $\text{NH}_3$, but $\text{AgI}$ is too insoluble to dissolve even in concentrated ammonia.
options.C: Correct. Both species have 10 electrons and are isoelectronic. $\text{NH}_4^+$ has 7 + 4 - 1 = 10 electrons and $\text{CH}_4$ has 6 + 4 = 10 electrons.
options.D: False on shape. The ammonium ion does contain one dative covalent bond ($\text{NH}_3$ donating to $\text{H}^+$), but its geometry is tetrahedral, not square planar.
